newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Parliamentary probe into CVRD seen in 15 days.
newsitem.headline: Parliamentary probe into CVRD seen in 15 days.

text.p: A Brazilian lower house deputy said a parliamentary inquiry into alleged irregularities in the privatization of state mining giant CVRD would be launched in 15 days, a local news agency said.

Deputy Miro Teixeira said 210 members of the Chamber of Deputies had already signed a petition calling for a Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry (CPI) into the upcoming CVRD sale, more than the 171 signatures needed in the lower house, Agencia Estado said.
Teixeira did not mention, however, how many signatures have been forthcoming in the Senate, where support of one- third of senators is needed for the CPI to go ahead, Agencia Estado said.

The probe will focus on allegations that ties between U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch and South African mining conglomerate Anglo American Corp constitute a conflict of interest in the privatization process.

Merrill Lynch acted as a consultant in the CVRD privatization and owns a South African brokerage which acts as a sponsoring broker for Anglo American, which is likely to bid in the sell-off of a 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares.
Teixeira said there was strong evidence that the CVRD tender document was conceived in such a way as to favor Anglo American in the privatization process.
Merrill Lynch has rejected the accusations.
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
